triple_constraint.governing_guidelines: California Welfare & Institutions Code Chapter 11 (Elder and Dependent Adult Civil Protection Act, WIC §§15600-15675); Probate Code §859 (double damages); Civil Code §3294 (punitive damages standard)
triple_constraint.standards_of_creation: Five-layer bar; no stubs; ADAM+EVE dual witness; verified live-fetched statutes
triple_constraint.standard_of_care: Elders and dependent adults subject to financial abuse often cannot advocate for themselves — the legal system's enhanced remedies exist precisely because the abuse occurs in relationships of trust and dependency

elder_definition: WIC §15610.27: any person residing in California, 65 years of age or older

cross_citizen_refs.CA_Probate_Conservatorship_Litigator: Conservatorship as instrument of elder financial abuse; Hillberg/mother may be under financial control instruments
cross_citizen_refs.CA_Insurance_Compliance_Litigator: State Farm policy; insurance agent as mandated reporter under §15630
cross_citizen_refs.US_Federal_Civil_Rights_Litigator: §1983 — state actor involvement in elder financial abuse scheme
cross_citizen_refs.CA_Healthcare_Fraud_Litigator: Medical decision override of elder; healthcare fraud connected to financial abuse

critical_financial_finding.prob_859_double_damages: PROB §859 provides TWICE THE VALUE of property taken in bad faith or through elder financial abuse (§15610.30). Applies to the Hillberg State Farm/Northern Trust scheme.
critical_financial_finding.wic_15657_5_mandatory_fees: WIC §15657.5(a): if financial abuse proven by preponderance, attorney's fees are MANDATORY — not discretionary. No §377.34 cap if clear and convincing recklessness/fraud/malice.
critical_financial_finding.representative_liability: WIC §15610.30(d): conservator, trustee, and attorney-in-fact ARE 'representatives' — their acts of financial abuse are covered as direct perpetrators, not just agents
